requirements:
## Cover the requirements

Before implementation, connect each requirement to observable evidence: normal behavior, boundaries,
validation priority and state after failure. Keep this map concise in scratch notes or tests. Choose a
requirement-based failing check before its fix; derive expectations independently of the implementation.
Supplied examples may cover only part of the contract. Check uncovered requirements with focused tests
or an explicit code review, and distinguish tested behavior from assumptions in the final report.
resources:
## Preserve resource and action contracts

Use callees' declared actions, including cleanup performed inside helpers. Do not narrow action bounds
from the operations visibly spelled in the caller alone. Identify borrowed versus owned resources.
Prefix try does not roll back or release anything: capture outcomes before teardown, release owned
resources on every relevant return, and preserve the original failure when cleanup is secondary.
Verify state after an error and repeated invocation, not just the returned value.
finish:
## Finish against evidence

Identify the task's acceptance gate before editing. Use remaining time and observed check duration to
plan required verification and a concise handoff. After required checks and requirement review, if no
concrete contract gap remains, stop editing and report the evidence. A passing sample alone is not full
acceptance. Further edits need an identified unmet requirement or observed defect. Do not weaken tests
or skip required verification to meet a deadline; report an incomplete check honestly when time runs out.
